anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet (mcu.kicad_sch), the USB-C receptacle J12 VBUS pin (A4) is drawn with BOTH a '+5V' power symbol and a 'VBUS' global label on the same node. The same 'VBUS' global label appears on the Power sheet at U5 OUT (pin 1), C11, TP1 and U8 IN (pin 3), while U5 IN2 (pin 2) is labelled '+5V'. Attaching the VBUS label to the USB VBUS pin therefore merges the USB input rail (+5V) with the post-mux internal rail (VBUS).
anomalies.expected: The two rails must be separate nets. The spec states the USB connector feeds the '+5V' net into the mux input, and that the mux output net 'VBUS' is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux'. J12 pin A4 should carry only '+5V' (the mux IN2 net), never 'VBUS'.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (tiles 1/4 and 2/4): J12 pin A4 shows a '+5V' power symbol and a red 'VBUS' global label on the same wire; power.kicad_sch (tile 1/4): U5 pin 1 OUT = 'VBUS', U5 pin 2 IN2 = '+5V'
J12 (USB_C_Receptacle_USB2.0_14P) VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) → +5V net → U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2).

outputs a single OUT (pins 1/1_1/8/8_1) onto the VBUS net (the board's internal, unregulated/pre-buck rail — note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux).

anomalies.impact: The mux output is hard-tied to its IN2 and to the USB-C VBUS pin, bypassing the TPS2121 arbitration. When the 12 V barrel jack is connected, ~12 V appears on the USB-C VBUS pin and on U5 IN2, back-powering any attached host/device (a USB-spec violation and potential damage) and shorting the 5 V and pre-buck rails together.

anomalies.observed: A 2-pin screw terminal J5 is wired between the HEATER control net (ESP32 GPIO1 / U6 IN·DIAG_EN, 3.3 V logic) and GND, alongside D2/R3.
anomalies.expected: The spec's net-by-net trace of the HEATER net lists only GPIO1, U6 IN/DIAG_EN, and the D2+R3 indicator — no user screw terminal. A field-accessible screw terminal should not sit on the 3.3 V heater-control signal (if it is meant as a heater output it belongs on the switched U6 OUT net feeding J6); shorting J5 pulls GPIO1 to GND and disables the heater.

evidence.quote: mcu.kicad_sch (tile 1/4): J5 Screw_Terminal_01x02 pin 2 → 'HEATER', pin 1 → GND
A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the HEATER net, so the heater output doubles as a visual "heater on" indicator at the board level

anomalies.impact: A user wire/jumper on J5 shorts the heater drive line to ground, preventing the heater from ever turning on; if J5 was intended as a heater power terminal it would instead expose a 3.3 V logic signal.

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: the USB-C VBUS pin (J12.A4) carries the 'VBUS' global label in addition to '+5V', bridging the USB input rail to the post-mux pre-buck rail that the spec explicitly requires to be distinct — back-feeding 12 V onto the USB connector and defeating the power mux. A secondary, lower-confidence finding is the un-described screw terminal J5 tied across the 3.3 V heater-control net.
